title: Here’s what you can expect from The Wild Party at New York City Cente...
transcript: I just got back from seeing The Wild Party at New York City Center. This is the latest show from their encores series, where they spotlight older musicals that haven't been seen in a little while and revive them with an all star cast and a full orchestra. And while these are traditionally concert stagings with very minimal sets and actors reading from binders, this one feels like more or less a fully staged production. And it is incredibly impressive what they were able to put together with just 10 days of rehearsals. Actors are entirely off book, I did not see a single script. And this is really difficult music, so that is no easy feat. There is also some great choreography, some gorgeous lighting. And while the set is still minimal, the entire show takes place in one apartment, so it doesn't necessarily feel limited. And while typically I would say that this could be a sign that the show is looking to move towards Broadway, I don't really know that this show could ever be commercially viable, despite its strong performances. Especially from Jordan Donica, who I think steals the show. Broadway legend Tanya Pinkins, who actually originated the role of Kate in the original production, now playing Dolores in this production with a really great number in Act 2. You also have people like Jasmine Amy Rogers, Adrienne Warren, Lesli Margherita, Jelani Aladdin. This is one of the most stacked casts that City Center has. Ever had. And very sexy. Like there is a lot of sex in the show. So if you are a prude, maybe stay away from this one. But I say all that to say, while this is a very sleek, well directed, well performed production, you can see why the show wasn't a huge hit on Broadway. It gets off to a pretty slow start, the characters are hard to invest in and it just feels a little bit bloated. Especially because this production does not have an intermission, so it is just over two hours straight. There is some really great music by Michael John LaChiusa and it's very different from the sound that we are used to hearing from city center shows, which tends to stick to that golden age orchestral sound. This score is much more jazzy and brassy and I really loved seeing them expand their horizons Musically with the show. Encores was made for shows that aren't perfect but still have a lot to admire, and I think that Wild Party falls squarely in that category.
classificationReason: Creator attended ('just got back from seeing The Wild Party at New York City Center') and shares opinions on the staging, choreography, and performances including Jordan Donica and Tonya Pinkins.
